title: Optimal truthful approximation for multi-hospital kidney exchange
area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
formal: Determine the optimal worst-case approximation ratio of randomized truthful-in-expectation mechanisms for two-way kidney exchange with arbitrarily many hospitals that may hide vertices and internally match their remaining patients.
definitions: Definitions and model details remain incomplete. Define hospital utilities, allowed internal matching and deviations, zero-optimum cases and the mechanism's information; preserve the unrestricted hospital count.

Exact determination also qualifies; the approximation does not establish an associated exact conjecture. This is a provisional candidate, not a completed benchmark specification. import_provenance.original_title: The optimal truthful approximation for multi-hospital kidney exchange
import_provenance.original_statement: What is the best worst-case approximation ratio attainable by a randomized mechanism truthful in expectation for two-way kidney exchange with arbitrarily many hospitals? Hospitals own vertex sets, maximize their own matched patients, and may hide vertices and match them internally with their remaining unmatched vertices.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The paper gives factor 2 and a randomized impossibility bound of 8/7; the deterministic factor-2 lower bound does not settle the randomized question. The target concerns two-cycles and unrestricted hospital counts, not the better-understood two-hospital case.
